title: CSS fundamentals: selectors, cascade, box model
intro: CSS controls how HTML looks and how elements are sized, spaced, and positioned. In this lesson, you will learn the core ideas behind CSS selectors, the cascade, the box model, units, colours, variables, and browser tools for understanding why a style is or is not being applied.
takeaways: CSS selects HTML elements and applies declarations that control their presentation, sizing, spacing, and behaviour.
Prefer reusable classes and simple selectors rather than relying heavily on IDs, inline styles, or overly specific selectors.
The cascade considers factors such as origin, specificity, source order, and inheritance when deciding which styles win.
The box model consists of content, padding, border, and margin; `box-sizing: border-box` makes declared dimensions easier to reason about.
DevTools Styles and Computed panes help you understand which CSS rules apply and what final values the browser calculates.

quiz.question: What does the `.card` part of this CSS rule represent: `.card { padding: 20px; }`?
options: A CSS selector targeting the card class
quiz.explanation: `.card` is a class selector that matches elements whose class includes `card`.

quiz.question: If two matching selectors have equal specificity, which declaration normally wins?
options: The declaration that appears later in source order
The declaration with the shorter property name
The declaration from the first rule
quiz.explanation: When relevant declarations have equal specificity and other factors do not differ, the later declaration wins.

quiz.question: What does `box-sizing: border-box` change?
options: It includes padding and border within the declared width and height
quiz.explanation: With border-box, the declared width and height include the element's content, padding, and border.

quiz.question: Which unit is relative to the root element's font size?
quiz.explanation: The rem unit is relative to the font size of the root element.

quiz.question: Which DevTools pane is most useful for seeing the final calculated value of a CSS property?
quiz.explanation: The Computed pane shows the final values the browser calculates after applying CSS rules, inheritance, and related processing.

exercise.title: Style a profile card
exercise.task: Style the provided profile card using CSS in the existing `style` element. The tests expect `.card` to use `box-sizing: border-box`, have at least 16px of padding on every side, have a visible solid border, and have a maximum width that keeps its rendered width at or below 400px. Define a CSS custom property named `--accent` on `:root` and use it as the `.button` background colour; the button must have no underline. Finally, remove the default top margin from the card's `h2`.

exercise.hint: Start with `:root { --accent: ...; }`. Then give `.card` `box-sizing: border-box`, a `max-width` of 400px or less, padding, and a solid border. Use `background-color: var(--accent)` on `.button`, `text-decoration: none`, and `.card h2 { margin-top: 0; }`.

tests.name: The card uses the border box model
The card has padding and a border
tests.code: const style = getComputedStyle(document.querySelector('.card')); return ['paddingTop', 'paddingRight', 'paddingBottom', 'paddingLeft'].every(prop => parseFloat(style[prop]) >= 16) && parseFloat(style.borderTopWidth) >= 1 && style.borderTopStyle === 'solid';

tests.name: The card has a maximum width
tests.code: const card = document.querySelector('.card'); const style = getComputedStyle(card); return style.maxWidth !== 'none' && card.getBoundingClientRect().width <= 400.5;

tests.name: The button uses the accent variable
tests.code: const root = document.documentElement; const button = document.querySelector('.button'); const accent = getComputedStyle(root).getPropertyValue('--accent').trim(); const probe = document.createElement('div'); probe.style.backgroundColor = `var(--accent)`; root.appendChild(probe); const resolved = getComputedStyle(probe).backgroundColor; probe.remove(); return accent !== '' && getComputedStyle(button).backgroundColor === resolved;

tests.name: The heading and button styles are correct
tests.code: const heading = document.querySelector('.card h2'); const button = document.querySelector('.button'); return parseFloat(getComputedStyle(heading).marginTop) === 0 && getComputedStyle(button).textDecorationLine === 'none';
